text:
Marta Lopez: Quick policy check  Team question: How do we handle partial-day PTO that overlaps a regional public holiday? Example: employee in EMEA wants a half day Fri 2026-05-01 but that's also a regional bank holiday PM. Do we count as 0.5 PTO or 0 PTO?

Ravi Kumar: Finance prefers 0 PTO if the local law treats the public holiday as full-day statutory. But we need manager attestation and the employee's local holiday calendar. Also payroll needs a `holiday_adjustment` tag so accruals don't double-count.

Sam Wu: From manager side: I'd expect employees to take the non-holiday portion as PTO (so 0.5) unless company policy explicitly grants the holiday. We should document per-region rules.

Lina Chen: Practically we've seen confusion when part-timers cross timezones for global sprints. Can we require the employee to choose timezone context `--local` in the request so the bot knows which holiday calendar to check?

people-ops-bot: Auto-check: requested date 2026-05-01 overlaps `france: Labor Day (all-day)`. Recommended: mark as `holiday_override=false`. Ask manager to confirm whether to consume PTO. Suggested command: `@people-ops-bot request-pto --date 2026-05-01 --partial=AM --tz=Europe/Paris`

Marta Lopez: We'll standardize: if the holiday is statutory in the employee's location and the overlap covers the hours requested, PTO should not be consumed. If only part of the requested hours fall on the holiday, PTO covers the remainder. People Ops will publish a short table per country.

Ravi Kumar: For payroll, require a field `payroll_tag` with one of: `paid_holiday`, `pto_used`, `unpaid_leave`. That prevents accidental double-pay. Also: flag requests that change accrual month boundaries for manual review.

Sam Wu: What about blackout weeks? If the partial-day is during a release blackout, do we still allow auto approval? My vote: block auto-approval and require manager + eng lead ack.

people-ops-bot: Blackout check: 2026-05-01 is within release-freeze 2026-05-01..2026-05-05 for core infra. Result: manager approval required. Reply `approve`/`deny`.

Lina Chen: Also consider part-time FTE rounding rules. For 0.5 FTE employees we currently round accruals monthly; request spanning month boundaries should pro-rate. People Ops: can we add a note to the PTO form: "cross-month requests may be pro-rated"?

Marta Lopez: Yes. We'll update the form and add an FAQ entry. Example guidance we'll publish:

```
If a requested PTO window overlaps a local statutory holiday that covers the requested hours, PTO will not be deducted.
If only part of the PTO request overlaps the holiday, only the non-holiday hours are deducted.
Part-time employees: accrual pro-rating applies when PTO spans month boundaries; payroll will calculate exact hours.
Requests in release blackout windows require manager + eng lead approval; bot will block auto-approve.
```

Ravi Kumar: One operational ask: bot should emit the payroll payload with `payroll_tag` and `accrual_month` fields. Example payload snippet:

```
employee: lina.chen
date: 2026-05-01
partial: AM
tz: Europe/Paris
holiday_detected: true
payroll_tag: paid_holiday
accrual_month: 2026-05
```

Marta Lopez: Good. We'll also add a short escalation path for contested cases: people-ops -> payroll -> legal.

Sam Wu: Sounds good. When's the update going live?

Marta Lopez: I'll post the per-country table + updated form by Monday 09:00. I'll add the FAQ and sample Slack command examples.

people-ops-bot: Reminder: Marta scheduled update post for 2026-04-27 09:00. Calendar invite sent.
